title: Session-tagged proration orchestrator for cross-model multi-route billing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a resilient orchestration job that produces reconciled, per-tenant billing rows for sessions that traverse multiple model routes and cost tiers. The job will: 1) ingest real-time usage events (streamed Kafka + S3 backlog), 2) consolidate events by session_id and session_tag, 3) apply route-aware proration logic when a single logical user session is served by multiple model variants (different per-token costs and quantization), 4) smooth and probabilistically attribute late-arrival events to prevent cost volatility, and 5) emit idempotent ledger rows suitable for chargeback and invoice generation. Deliverables: - A multi-stage Spark/Flink pipeline that supports streaming and bounded backfill modes - Deterministic proration algorithm with configurable decay window and confidence heuristics - Idempotent output format with stable keys and lineage metadata - Backfill plan and safe-merge path for existing ledgers - Dashboards and alerts for reconciliation delta, backfill progress, and attribution confidence
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline emits per-tenant ledger rows with stable idempotency keys and lineage for all sessions in the test tenant cohort
Proration unit tests cover split-route scenarios and show <=0.5% reconciliation drift versus golden dataset
Late-arrival smoothing reduces per-day ledger volatility by >=40% in the replayed backlog sample
Rollout can be toggled per-tenant and includes a canary that validates billing-exactness before full merge
implementation_notes: Event enrichment: attach route_cost_id, model_variant_id, and sequence_offset at ingress to ensure deterministic grouping
State windowing: use session-tag TTL + adaptive decay (configurable) to bound memory and backfill scope
Idempotency: key = sha256(tenant|session_tag|window_start|route_cost_bucket) to allow safe replays
Backfill strategy: run bounded batch jobs with ordering guarantees, mark backlog segments as 'reconciled' to avoid double-apply
Observability: emit reconciliation_delta metric (per-tenant, per-day) and attribution_confidence histogram
risks_and_tradeoffs: Aggressive smoothing reduces short-term cost signal fidelity for fraud detection; tradeoff controlled via decay window
Per-session grouping increases state size; mitigated by TTL and probabilistic eviction policy for very long-lived sessions
Deterministic keys require stable upstream route_cost_id — we must coordinate with routing service to avoid churn
testing_plan: Unit tests for proration math and late-arrival weight decay
Integration test against synthetic multi-route workload stored in S3 (100k sessions)
Shadow run for 7 days alongside current ledger generator for two pilot tenants
End-to-end reconciliation check comparing shadowed outputs with billing sandbox
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Run pipeline in dry-run mode and surface reconciliation deltas to console dashboard (1 tenant)
Phase 2: Canary write path for subset of tenant traffic (10 tenants) and manual verification
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with continuous monitoring and automatic rollback on delta threshold breach
Phase 4: Backfill historical 90-day window using bounded batches and reconcile into canonical ledger
